name: August Wi-Fi Smart Lock Gen 4 (US)

radios.note: Built-in Wi-Fi for remote and voice control; Bluetooth for local operation and for talking to HomeKit.

matter.note: No official Matter statement found. A Best Buy Canada spec sheet lists Matter as unsupported, but retailer data is not enough to mark it 'no'.

apple_home.note: HomeKit over Bluetooth. Controlling it away from home needs an Apple home hub (Apple TV, HomePod or iPad). No Home Key mentioned.

google_home.note: Google Assistant integration needs the lock on Wi-Fi.

alexa.note: Needs Wi-Fi. Voice unlock requires setting a PIN.

smartthings.note: An older August page lists Samsung SmartThings, but we could not confirm it for the 4th-gen lock on a current page.

home_assistant.note: The August integration lists the Wi-Fi Smart Lock (Gen 4) as working with no Connect Bridge. Gen 4 battery readings are often wrong in Home Assistant.

hubRequired.note: Wi-Fi is built in; August says no bridge is needed. Remote HomeKit use still needs an Apple home hub.

localControl.note: Bluetooth control from the app is local, but no source confirms local control through any smart home platform.

lockFit.note: Mounts over the interior side of your existing deadbolt, so your outside hardware and keys stay.

keypad.note: No keypad on the lock; Yale/August sell keypad versions as separate products.

power.note: August's FAQ says two 3V CR123 lithium cells, with about 3 months of life under typical Wi-Fi use. Retailers disagree (some say 4 AA), and Home Assistant's page calls the batteries lithium-ion.

summary: August's 4th-gen lock sits over the inside of your existing deadbolt and has Wi-Fi built in, so no separate bridge is required. It works with Alexa, Google Assistant and Apple Home (via Bluetooth), and Home Assistant lists it as supported. Remote Siri control needs an Apple TV, HomePod or iPad as a home hub, and the lock has no Matter listing.
caveats: Battery life is short: August cites about 3 months with Wi-Fi in typical use.
Away-from-home control through Apple Home needs an Apple TV, HomePod or iPad acting as a home hub.
Home Assistant often shows wrong battery levels for this model.
No keypad on the lock itself; keypads are sold separately.
